Re: Follow-up on Meta TPP Internews Report?
[contact omitted] Ulvi Ismayil Tuesday, April 30, 2024 at 10:28:14 PM Eastern Daylight Time
To: [contact omitted] Vera Zakem
Cc: [contact omitted] Cara Thanassi, [contact omitted] Chioma Ayogu, [contact omitted] Carrie Mitchell,
[contact omitted] Chantal Agarwal, [contact omitted] Daniella Burgi-Palomino, [contact omitted] Drusilla
Menaker, [contact omitted] Gary Bland, [contact omitted] Kayla Goodson, [contact omitted] Lorri Anne Meils,
[contact omitted] Susan Abbott
Hi Daniella et al,
All I remember from that meeting and further conversations with Internews is that Meta broke its ties with Internews when
this report was published. Internews even noticed that some NGOs that were previously in a coalition with Internews
stopped answering emails. I'm not surprised that Meta's reaction to that question was short.
Best regards,
Ulvi Ismayil,
Senior Media Advisor
USAID | Washington, DC
Bureau for Democracy, Human Rights, and Governance (DRG)
[opaque block]
[contact omitted]
On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 8:52 PM Vera Zakem <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Thanks Cara! Just from Agency perspective,1 am not comfortable in pressing on this further at this time.
On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 4:44 PM Cara Thanassi <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Thanks Chioma et al- we'll certainly loop in GC as LAC considers next steps on this.
Cara L. Thanassi
Democracy Specialist for Latin America and the Caribbean
USAID Bureau for Latin America and the Caribbean, Democracy and Human Rights Team
Cell: [opaque block]
On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 6:39 PM Chioma Ayogu <[contact omitted]>wrote:
ATTORNEY CLIENT PRIVILEGED
I would also add that with respect to ongoing discussions with Meta or others, USAID will need to continue to tread
carefully and continue to ensure that it is not and is not perceived to be putting pressure on them to change
policies. My understanding is that USAID has already asked about issues with the program and received answers
from Meta. If USAID is not asking new questions or presenting new undiscussed issues the risk that USAID's
repeated pointed questions about the same program may be viewed as coercive. Further, the talking points for
such discussions would need to be carefully reviewed by GC to make sure they do not cross legal redlines.
These types of discussions should be conducted consistent with FAQ #16 of the GC guidance.
Warm regards,
Chioma
CHIOMA AYOGU
Senior Counsel
Office of the General Counsel, Development, Democracy and Economics (GC/DDE)
Clients: DRG Bureau
[contact omitted]
